items.hook: Mud from Roman wells in Belgium yields ancient DNA that matches and extends excavated remains.
items.summary: DNA extracted from sediment in disused Roman wells at Harelbeke, Belgium, reproduced most crop and livestock signals known from excavation and added environmental species that older methods missed. It also placed a pig within the European mitochondrial lineage. This is one site, and counting taxa cannot show how much each food mattered.
items.title: Sedimentary ancient DNA expands bioarchaeological evidence and interpretation at Roman Harelbeke

items.hook: Models project 31 major tree pests and pathogens shifting north, threatening boreal forests by 2041 to 2080.
items.summary: Species distribution models for 31 damaging tree pests and pathogens predict a consistent northward shift under climate scenarios, raising risk in northern temperate and boreal forests and lowering it in places like southern Europe. Temperature and precipitation of the warmest quarter and driest month were key drivers. These models use climate suitability alone and do not simulate dispersal, host availability or control.
items.title: Climate change drives northward range shifts in invasive forest pests and pathogens

items.hook: In mice, sleep restores neuron autophagy that waking suppresses, and sleep-timed stimulation cut amyloid.
items.summary: In mouse cortex, long wakefulness reduced neuronal autophagy and sleep quickly restored it. Closed-loop optogenetic stimulation of lysosomal acidification only during sleep reduced amyloid pathology in 5xFAD mice, while wake-timed stimulation worsened it. The results are from mice and a single Alzheimer model, and some mechanisms are described as putative.
items.title: Sleep promotes neuronal autophagy for intracellular clearance

items.hook: Partial reprogramming trades rejuvenation for recovery differently in each human cell type.
items.summary: Researchers briefly reprogrammed human fibroblasts, T cells and aortic endothelial cells and tracked recovery. Endothelial cells recovered identity and improved vascular function, T cells recovered only from shallow reprogramming, and fibroblasts recovered incompletely. TOX was a shared dependency but its downstream programs differed by lineage. The work uses cultured cells, so benefits in living tissue are untested.
items.title: Partial reprogramming reveals lineage-specific uncoupling of rejuvenation, function, and recoverability in human cells

items.hook: A five-strain E. coli community learns an association, holds it as memory, and erases it on command.
items.summary: Five engineered E. coli strains share one quorum-sensing signal that serves as the memory, and together they showed classic associative learning: after pairing, a stimulus that was silent before triggered a response. The memory survived a medium exchange and could be erased. It is a lab demonstration in a culture with a simple model, not a durable or general memory system.
items.title: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System

items.hook: An RNA interference circuit with feedback holds human cells near criticality, with power-law bursts.
items.summary: A synthetic circuit in human cells, where mRNAs queue for shared RNA interference machinery and a repressor gives negative feedback, kept the system near a critical point. Theory and simulation predicted scale-free bursts, and measured single-cell fluorescence followed power-law distributions. The evidence is in engineered circuits in cell lines, so natural cells remain a possibility only.
items.title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit

items.hook: The first full-length structure of human hephaestin shows a membrane-anchored homodimer at 2.3 angstroms.
items.summary: Hephaestin helps move iron out of gut cells. The authors purified the full-length human protein and solved its cryo-EM structure, a stable homodimer with a negatively charged funnel leading to the substrate site that may capture Fe2+. The membrane helices are less well resolved, and how it works with ferroportin was not tested.
items.title: Structure of human hephaestin reveals a homodimer anchored to the cell membrane

items.hook: A 25-minute paper-strip test detects RNA of the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola strain
items.summary: Researchers designed isothermal amplification primers for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus strain and read the result on a lateral flow strip. The primers reacted only with the target RNA, not with other filoviruses, arboviruses or human cells, and worked down to 10^3 copies per reaction. Testing used synthetic RNA and viral RNA in the lab, not patient samples, so real-world accuracy is unknown.
items.title: Reverse Transcription Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Combined with Lateral Flow Assay (RT-LAMP-LFA) for Rapid Detection of the 2026 Bundibugyo Virus (BDBV) Outbreak Strain

items.hook: Broader Spike-recognizing T cell receptor repertoires predicted fewer symptomatic COVID cases after a booster

readout.label: Hazard ratio, symptomatic infection, higher breadth

items.summary: Using participants' HLA types and T cell receptor sequences from a third-dose vaccine trial, the team estimated how many Spike fragments each person's T cells could recognize. Higher breadth went with lower risk of symptomatic infection, even after accounting for antibodies and interferon-gamma responses. It is an observational association in one trial, so it does not show that breadth causes protection.
items.title: Personalized HLA-aware TCR measure predicts the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection following booster vaccination

items.hook: Patch-clamp tests resolved 64 of 201 uncertain long QT gene variants as likely harmful or benign
items.summary: The team measured 303 KCNH2 variants with automated patch-clamp electrophysiology and trafficking assays, then calibrated the results against known benign and pathogenic variants. This let them reclassify 64 of 201 variants of uncertain significance and build an open database. Predictions matched patient QT data for 82.9% of pathogenic variants, and the assays use cell models rather than patient heart tissue.
items.title: Nationwide Functional Profiling Enables Clinical Reclassification of KCNH2 Variants in the French LQT2 Population

items.hook: A trained detector finds heart structures in echo images where general AI models find 3% or fewer
items.hook_turn: where general AI models find 3% or fewer
items.summary: General and medical vision-language models almost never located cardiac structures in echocardiograms. EchoLens, a detector trained on expert-annotated structures and Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% of structures and matched a blinded expert on placement. Training data came from a small patient group, and external checks relied on two physicians judging detections.
items.title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram

items.hook: Some bacterial tRNAs read the codon CGG as tryptophan, not arginine, as computation had predicted
items.summary: Computational predictions suggested some bacteria decode the arginine codon CGG as tryptophan. In an E. coli cell-free system, candidate tRNAs from distant bacteria restored fluorescence and enzyme activity, and mass spectrometry showed tryptophan in place of arginine. Proteomics of Anaerococcus prevotii agreed. Direct evidence covers one native species and a test-tube system, not living cells of other predicted bacteria.
items.title: Sense-to-sense changes in bacterial genetic codes: Experimental validation by cell-free translation and native-host proteomics

items.hook: A new method maps 24 cell types continuously across the human cortex from gene expression data
items.summary: RIDGE combines regional reference data with cortex-wide gene expression maps to estimate where 24 cortical cell types sit. The maps held up across pipelines and reference datasets and reproduced a known sensory-to-allocortical gradient. The cell-type distributions are statistical estimates inferred from transcriptomics, not direct cell counts.
items.title: A spatially continuous cell-type atlas reveals multiscale organization of the human cortex

items.hook: Campylobacter's flagellar motor has exceptionally high torque and a linear torque-speed decline

readout.label: Stall torque, C. jejuni flagellar motor

items.summary: Single-motor measurements of Campylobacter jejuni showed a stall torque far above model bacteria and a roughly linear drop in torque with speed, unlike the biphasic curve in E. coli. Inferred active stator units averaged 11, fewer than the 17 seen structurally, and activity recovered quickly after proton motive force collapse. The linear trend was seen only over the measured speed range, and stator counts are inferred.
items.title: Torque generation and regulation in the flagellar motor of Campylobacter jejuni differ from those of model organisms

items.hook: Injectable implants spotted fentanyl overdose in rats and delivered naloxone in under 6 minutes

readout.label: Autonomous rescue time, fentanyl overdose in rats

items.summary: RES-Q pairs wearable sensors with needle-injectable autoinjectors that fire a jet of naloxone through scar tissue, with implants triggered by signals passed through the body. In rats, a wearable pulse sensor detected fentanyl overdose and set off rescue automatically. Swine tests covered only implant communication, and no human data exist.
items.title: A network of syringe-injectable bioelectronics for closed-loop therapeutic rescue

items.hook: Fragmented islet clusters survive low oxygen and controlled diabetes in mice for over 5 weeks
items.summary: Passing native islets through a mesh produced smaller clusters that tolerate low oxygen better and had less central necrosis after implantation. Rat versions in a thin alginate device controlled blood sugar in immune-competent diabetic mice for over 5 weeks at a modest dose. The study is short, in mice, and uses rat tissue, so human benefit is untested.
items.title: Engineered endocrine objects tolerate hypoxia in macroencapsulation devices and enable subcutaneous engraftment in diabetic mice

items.hook: An engineered compact CRISPR nuclease edits monkey liver at lower doses than Cas9 therapies

readout.label: Editing activity gain in human cells

items.summary: Screening tens of thousands of Cas12e protein and guide variants yielded X-Editor, which is over 100-fold more active in human cells. Delivered by lipid nanoparticle to monkey liver, it edited two targets at lower doses than published preclinical Cas9 data, with no off-target edits found in human hepatocytes. The comparison is to other studies rather than head to head, and only two targets were tested.
items.title: Comprehensive engineering of the CasX-Editor to generate a therapeutically optimized genome editor

items.hook: Viral RNA from Ebola-family viruses is detected by PCR directly in 2 microliters of blood

readout.label: Detection level for Ebola-family RNA in blood

items.summary: By combining blood-tolerant chemistry, RNase inhibition and longer-wavelength fluorescence, the authors ran qPCR without extracting nucleic acid first. They detected hepatitis B DNA and RNA of hepatitis C, Bundibugyo, Ebola and Sudan viruses, with a portable instrument giving results in an hour. Tests used blood spiked with nucleic acid standards, not intact virus or patient samples.
items.title: Direct Whole-Blood PCR for Molecular Diagnostics

items.hook: Axolotl cells that switch off Sox9 rebuild limb skeleton better than cells that keep it on
items.hook_turn: better than cells that keep it on
items.summary: Fate mapping in axolotl limbs showed that Sox9-expressing cells either kept the gene on and became cartilage, or turned it off and became other tissues such as dermal fibroblasts. During regeneration, cells that had turned Sox9 off contributed far more to new skeleton and could switch it back on. Findings come from one salamander species and genetic labeling.
items.title: Reversible expression of a cartilage 'master regulator' during axolotl limb development and regeneration

items.hook: Germ granule shape and placement in worm germlines predict an animal's age
items.summary: In C. elegans, P granules and Mutator foci change in form, position and association with age. Features from single nuclei trained an image-based clock, GG-Clock, that predicts chronological age, and intermittent fasting shifted its output younger. The work is limited to worms, and the open-source GGProfiler tool is not yet shown on other species.
items.title: Germ Granule Remodeling Reveals Germline Age in Caenorhabditis elegans

items.hook: Single neurons in speech motor cortex carry information about sentence structure and meaning.
items.summary: Neurons in speech motor cortex carry signals about how sentences are built, not just the sounds and movements of speech. Implanted electrode arrays in three BrainGate2 participants recorded activity during sentences, word lists, and nonword versions of each, and the stimulus type could be decoded. Semantic categories were decodable in two larger datasets. Only three people took part in the main task, all with implants for clinical reasons.
items.title: Sentence-level neural dynamics in speech motor cortex

items.hook: A living nerve conduit seeded with Schwann cells restored motor function across long nerve gaps in rodents.
items.summary: The team built a tube mimicking nerve layers: a hydrogel bilayer, ferroelectric polymer stripes with nano-grooves, and living Schwann cells that release growth factors. In rats or mice with long nerve gaps, it boosted blood vessel growth, axon outgrowth, and myelin repair, with no neuroma. Results come from rodent models and a preprint; the claim of unprecedented recovery has not been tested in larger animals or people.
items.title: Bioinspired living nerve conduit with coupled physiological signals enables functional recovery of peripheral nerve

items.hook: People with long COVID show weaker antibody quality and CD4 T-cell responses to herpesviruses.
items.summary: Long COVID patients had lower early antibody avidity and weaker CD4 T-cell responses against CMV and EBV than recovered controls, while overall antibody levels and CD8 responses were preserved or higher. The researchers profiled blood at 4, 8, and 24 months after infection. Lower EBV avidity tracked with poorer quality of life. The study shows association only and cannot say whether the immune change contributes to long COVID.
items.title: Altered herpesvirus-specific immune response is associated with long COVID

items.hook: AI-guided TB screening in Pune found about three times more confirmed cases per person screened.

readout.label: Rate ratio, confirmed TB yield, AI vs standard

items.summary: An AI tool that maps neighborhood TB risk sent screening teams to likelier areas, so they found more confirmed lung TB per person screened and cut cost per case by 66%. Total TB detection did not differ from the standard campaign, which also used mobile X-ray. The comparison used different time periods in the same four units, not a concurrent trial, and the confirmed-case counts were small (10 versus 9).
items.title: Geospatial AI targeting of tuberculosis active case finding in Pune, India: a quasi-experimental evaluation

items.hook: Cholera in Africa tracks El Nino in five regional patterns, with a projected surge in the east.
items.summary: Using 15 years of surveillance data from 30 countries, the authors grouped African countries into five zones where El Nino changes the timing, size, or length of cholera outbreaks. For the 2026-27 El Nino they project two to five times more cholera in Eastern Africa and the Horn than in neutral years. The projection depends on statistical and simulation models fitted to surveillance data, which may be uneven in quality across countries.
items.title: El Nino Southern Oscillation shapes cholera in Africa

items.hook: Repeated drug-induced torpor slowed bone tumor growth in mice and shielded healthy tissue from radiation.
items.summary: Five drug-induced torpor bouts, given every other day, strongly slowed osteosarcoma growth in female mice, and the effect lasted after the last bout. Irradiating mice during torpor controlled the tumors as well as irradiating normal-temperature mice, while ovarian follicle loss was lower. This was one tumor line in one mouse strain, all female, so it is far from showing benefit in people.
items.title: Synthetic Hibernation Suppresses Osteosarcoma Growth and Protects Normal Tissue from Radiation

items.hook: First high-resolution structure of a bacterial conjugation pilus tip reveals a gatekeeper protein.
items.summary: Bacteria pass DNA to each other through hair-like pili, and the structure of the tip had been unknown. The structure of the R388 pilus tip shows the protein VirB6 sitting at the apex as a gate, plus a previously unknown adhesin called KikA. The authors propose that VirB6 links contact with a recipient cell to opening the channel. The gating mechanism is inferred from a static structure of one system and has not been tested functionally here.
items.title: Conjugative pilus tip structure reveals convergence in secretion systems

items.hook: In human brain organoids, MECP2-mutant and healthy cells sort apart and wire together less.
items.summary: Rett syndrome organoids built from mixed healthy and MECP2-mutant cells showed genotype-dependent spatial patterning, and the two truncating and missense mutations differed. Calcium imaging found that healthy neuron pairs coupled more strongly than mutant or mixed pairs, and RNA sequencing pointed to altered GABA and neurexin-neuroligin signaling. The signaling changes are inferred computationally, and organoids only approximate a real developing brain.
items.title: Human cortical mosaicoids reveal impact on spatial organization and progressive loss of cross-genotype functional coupling in MECP2 mosaicism

items.hook: Inducing torpor in rats cut heart injury by about 40% in isolated hearts after blocked blood flow.

readout.label: Infarct size reduction, ex vivo rat heart

items.summary: Chemogenetic activation of a hypothalamic region put rats, which never enter torpor naturally, into a torpor-like state. Their hearts were then tested ex vivo with simulated heart attack injury, and infarct size fell by about 40%, even when the animal had not become cold. Phosphoproteomics suggested more survival signaling and less cell-death signaling. Protection was shown only in isolated hearts, not in living animals.
items.title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

items.hook: Most human-chimpanzee differences in DNA methylation arise in cis, and selection shaped some pathways.
items.summary: Comparing methylation in six cell types and human-chimp hybrid cells, the authors found that methylation differences between the species are driven mostly by nearby DNA changes rather than by diffusible factors. Pathways tied to speech, cognition, and hepatitis C susceptibility showed signs of lineage-specific selection on promoter methylation. Methylation and expression link only weakly overall, and the selection findings are statistical inferences, not direct tests.
items.title: Cis-regulation and natural selection in the evolution of human DNA methylation.

items.hook: A single oral dose of the actinide chelator HOPO 14-1 up to 7500 mg caused no serious harm in 42 adults.

readout.label: Highest single oral dose, no serious events

items.summary: In a phase 1 trial, 42 healthy adults took one oral dose from 100 to 7500 mg of a drug meant to remove radioactive actinides from the body. There were no serious adverse events; mild to moderate diarrhea, vomiting, headache, and fatigue were the main side effects, worst at high doses. Most of the drug left in feces. It was a single-site, nonrandomized safety study in healthy people, so it does not show that the drug removes contamination.
items.title: HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.

items.hook: A nanofiber scaffold lets stacked perovskite layers form large, tough films that detect x-rays well.
items.summary: Researchers used an electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber mesh as a scaffold to build freestanding perovskite films, over 99 wt% perovskite, in layers of different compositions. The mesh also passivates defects at interfaces. A 2D/3D film made this way detected x-rays below the medical standard limit. The demonstration is one device type, and long-term stability is not described.
items.title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer-by-Layer Integration.

items.hook: Oxygen layer stacking decides whether a sodium battery cathode keeps its high-voltage oxygen plateau.
items.summary: In a Na-Li-Mn-Ti oxide, the P3 stacking pattern supported reversible high-voltage oxygen redox, while the P2 pattern lost it as metals migrated and molecular oxygen formed. The team combined experiments with calculations. The finding concerns one composition, so it may not carry over to other cathodes.
items.title: Layer Stacking Structure Governed Transition-Metal Interlayer Migration for Reversible High-Voltage Oxygen Redox Plateau.

items.hook: A bambusuril-coated silica captures pertechnetate from seawater at femtomolar levels.
items.summary: Bambusuril macrocycles bind pertechnetate, a radioactive technetium ion, in water, and anchoring them on silica gave a solid extractant that works in seawater and in nuclear medicine generator solutions. It also released the captured ion into kit formulations. The tests used lab solutions, not real waste streams.
items.title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril-based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions.

items.hook: Boryl groups range from strong electron donors to strong acceptors, a new Hammett scale shows.
items.summary: The authors measured how boryl groups change the acidity of substituted benzoic acids and filled gaps with calculations to build a set of Hammett constants. Borates donate electrons strongly, while dihaloboranes withdraw them strongly. Some values are computed rather than measured.
items.title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis.

items.hook: Protonating sulfonamides with a weakly coordinating anion makes isolable, tunable strong organic acids.
items.summary: The team protonated many sulfonamides in the presence of the tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion, giving stable salts whose nitrogen protonation was confirmed by X-ray diffraction. The acids can be tuned and made chiral. Catalytic uses were shown on only a few reactions.
items.title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides.

items.hook: One copper-cobalt-cerium oxide catalyst both loads and releases hydrogen in carbazole carriers.
items.summary: A non-precious CuCoCeOx catalyst reshapes itself during reaction into Cu-CoOx interface sites that handle both hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of liquid organic hydrogen carriers. It took up 98.4% H2 and held steady for five cycles. Five cycles is short for judging durability.
items.title: Synergistic Cu-Co Sites Enabled Reversible H2 Storage and Release in Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers.

items.hook: An iridium catalyst with borane turns esters into crowded ethers, including deuterated versions.
items.summary: An iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex with borane dimethyl sulfide reduced esters to hindered ethers, including types that silane systems miss. Swapping in deuterated borane gave dideuterated ethers with 92 to 96% deuterium. Scope was shown on a substrate series, not on drug-scale production.
items.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α,α-Dideuterated Ethers.

items.hook: X-ray imaging shows nickel catalyst beds change oxidation state in moving fronts, not uniformly.
items.summary: Operando X-ray micro-imaging with fast absorption spectroscopy tracked nickel on three supports during dry methane reforming, at about 15 micrometers and 10 seconds. Temperature gradients left uneven oxidation, and reaction fronts moved in or out depending on the support. Results cover three catalysts in one reactor setup.
items.title: Operando X-Ray Micro-Imaging Reveals Spatiotemporal Evolution of the Oxidation State of Nickel During Dry Methane Reforming.

items.hook: Cationic-pocket COFs cut PFOA from 1000 to 3.85 ng per liter in 10 minutes.

readout.label: PFOA left after 10 min, batch test

items.summary: Covalent organic frameworks with closely spaced pairs of quaternary ammonium sites bind PFAS strongly, working on ten different PFAS. Flow operation reached 0.82 ng per liter. Tests used lab water, so real contaminated water with competing ions may perform differently.
items.title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water.
